hints.content:
###Step 1

The interior angle measures of a triangle add up to $180\degree$. Every right triangle includes one angle that measures $90\degree$. So the measures of the remaining two acute angles do indeed add up to $90\degree$.

In this triangle, those acute angles have the measures $m\angle B$ and $\theta$.

Step 1 is correct.

###Step 2

The definition of sine is $\sin(\theta)=\dfrac{\blueE{\text{opposite leg length}}}{\goldE{\text{hypotenuse length}}}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

So $\sin(\theta)=\dfrac{\blueE{AB}}{\goldE{BC}}$.

Step 2 is correct.

options.alt: A right triangle A B C. Angle B A C is a right angle. Angle A C B is theta. Side A C is adjacent to angle C. Side A B is opposite to angle C. Side B C is the hypotenuse

hints.content:
###Step 3

We know from step 1 that $m\angle B = 90\degree - \theta$.

The definition of cosine is $\cos(x)=\dfrac{\purpleD{\text{adjacent leg length}}}{\goldE{\text{hypotenuse length}}}$.



[[☃ image 1]]

So $\cos(90\degree - \theta)=\dfrac{\purpleD{AB}}{\goldE{BC}}$.

Ismail said that $\cos(90\degree-\theta)=\dfrac{AC}{BC}$, so step 3 is incorrect.

hints.content:
The first mistake in Ismail's proof: 

He used the wrong sides in his ratio for $\cos(90\degree-\theta)$.

question.content:
Ismail tried to prove that $\sin(\theta)=\cos(90\degree-\theta)$ using the following diagram. His proof is not correct.



[[☃ image 1]]

| Statement | Reason
-: | :- | :-
1 | $m\angle B =90\degree - \theta$ | The acute angles in a right triangle are complementary.
2 | $\sin(\theta)=\dfrac{AB}{BC}$ | Definition of sine.
3 | $\cos(90\degree-\theta)=\dfrac{AC}{BC}$ | Definition of cosine.
4 | $\sin(\theta)=\cos(90\degree-\theta)$ | Substitution

**What is the first mistake in Ismail's proof?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

choices.content: The measures of $\angle B$ and $\angle C$ add up to $180\degree$, not $90\degree$.
Ismail used the wrong sides in his ratio for $\sin(\theta)$.
Ismail used the wrong sides in his ratio for $\cos(90\degree-\theta)$.
Ismail substituted a value that wasn't equivalent to the one he replaced.
